components.basis: All three bounded subcomponents (GOAL-01..03) are covered at their stated hypotheses; the original note (prime/atomic undefined although Ryll-Nardzewski is stated) is discharged by def:p03-atomic-prime and the Ryll-Nardzewski discussion at classification-theory.tex 135-143.

evidence.label: def:p03-atomic-prime
evidence.note: Atomic (every finite tuple realizes an isolated complete type over the empty set) and prime (elementary embedding into every model) defined for a complete satisfiable T; isolated = principal complete type.

evidence.label: thm:p03-prime-atomic
evidence.note: States: countable M is prime iff atomic; T has a prime model iff isolated types dense in every S_n(T); countability restriction belongs to clause 1. Proof route described.

evidence.label: annex:p3.vaught.overview-prime
evidence.note: Overview proof: infinite-model relational case, function languages via graph bridge, finite-model case.

evidence.label: thm:p03-prime-atomic
evidence.note: Density criterion stated; prime-to-atomic direction obtained by omitting a nonisolated type.

evidence.label: thm:p03-vaught-unary-obstruction
evidence.note: A complete satisfiable theory (T_bits) in which every consistent one-variable formula is atomless and which has no prime or atomic model: density of isolated types is a real condition, not true of every complete theory.

components.basis: Prime, atomic and isolated are defined, and the complete, countable-language setting is fixed.

evidence.label: thm:p03-prime-atomic

evidence.label: def:p03-vaught-standing

evidence.label: def:p03-vaught-model-notions

components.basis: Omission is the stated mechanism for prime-implies-atomic and for density-gives-atomic. T_bits is a complete theory with no prime model, which separates the density criterion from any claim that every complete theory has one.

evidence.label: thm:p03-prime-atomic

evidence.label: annex:p3.vaught.prime-atomic
evidence.note: Prime implies atomic via the omission construction; density gives an atomic (hence prime) model via the simultaneous construction.
